A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HERO study and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The retained material can be matched despite appendix renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original Stable Diffusion fine-tuning experiments, task success rates, ablations, training-time measurements, and preference and content-safety transfer results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports aesthetic, diversity, and alignment measurements, training-progress curves, and human-feedback timing measurements.

M1.justification: The triplet-based representation learning, cosine-similarity rewards, DDPO/LoRA fine-tuning, and feedback-guided Gaussian-mixture sampling remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the network architecture are retained; Appendix G elaborates on existing mechanisms.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five tasks in Table 1 and the same personal-preference and content-safety transfer prompts. The additional metrics and timing measurements concern retained tasks and feedback activities.

E2.justification: SD-Pretrained, SD-Enhanced, DreamBooth, the D3PO hand-task comparison, and DDPO with PickScore-v1 are retained. The latter comparison moves from Appendix B.1 to C.1. The new metric comparisons introduce no additional comparator methods.

E3.justification: Appendix B substantially broadens evaluation beyond task success by adding ImageReward, CLIP-based in-batch diversity, and CLIP and BLIP alignment measurements for final samples and training progress. Appendix G adds timing measurements for binary feedback and best-image selection. Existing training and generation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original reward, representation, best-image-ratio, and DreamBooth-prompt analyses are retained. v2 adds substantial training-progress analysis of aesthetics, diversity, and alignment, plus an assessment of best-image selection overhead that directly examines the feedback-efficiency argument.

E5.justification: The eight-seed hand evaluation, three-seed task evaluation, and three-seed best-image-ratio analysis retain their reporting practices. Figure 8 adds error bars for new outcomes but specifies no new uncertainty estimator or changed repeated-run protocol.

E6.justification: Figures 8-9 add four metrics across five tasks and their training trajectories. Appendix G reports approximately 0.5 seconds per binary judgment, 3-10 seconds for best-image selection, and an estimated 1332 binary-label-equivalent hand-task effort. Original success rates remain unchanged. Figure 2 corrects the red-rose SD-Enhanced example from success to failure.

T1.justification: Propositions A.1-A.2, their assumptions and proofs, and the method equations are unchanged. Appendix B states the standard formula for an adopted diversity metric; it does not introduce a new theoretical definition or result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the two-component HERO contribution, roughly fourfold hand-task feedback-efficiency claim, small-budget task performance, and qualified transferability claims. The rewritten conclusion does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 connects declining diversity to stronger human guidance, interprets alignment metrics as evidence of convergence toward human intent, and argues that best-image selection adds modest labor. These extend existing tradeoff and efficiency discussions; the original applicability assumptions and transferability qualifications remain.

D1.justification: The abstract adds code and project access information. Appendix G newly reports hand-task update-count and batch-size comparisons: 144 updates with batch size 8 for HERO versus 500 with batch size 10 for D3PO. These are additional disclosures, without an established change to the retained implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Caron, He, Radford, Li, and von Rutte for contrastive-learning context and evaluation metrics. Appendix G distinguishes HERO's human-supervised triplet learning from unsupervised contrastive learning. The main related-work section and overall research positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 updates the title, publication header, and correspondence information, adds acknowledgments, and locally rewrites ablation discussion and the conclusion. New appendix sections are inserted and existing appendices renumbered, while most wording and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two four-panel metric figures, reduces Figure 3's display size, and adjusts table sizing and placement. The original appendix image grids are retained as Figures 10-15 instead of Figures 8-13. These are localized additions and layout adjustments rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a fuller assessment of quality and diversity tradeoffs and estimates best-image selection effort omitted from v1's binary-feedback count. It also corrects Figure 2 and supplies code access information. The gains are limited by incompletely specified new error bars and timing measurements, while Figure 9 does not uniformly support the claim that alignment consistently improves.
